lead: Not every problem at sea is a MAYDAY. PAN-PAN asks for help when nobody is in immediate danger, and SÉCURITÉ warns other vessels of a hazard. Choose the right word and the right stations listen, with the right priority.

sections.title: How bad is it, and for whom?

qa.q: What is the difference between MAYDAY, PAN-PAN and SÉCURITÉ?
qa.a: MAYDAY is for **grave and imminent danger** to a vessel or a life; PAN-PAN when you need help urgently but nobody is in that danger yet; SÉCURITÉ when you need nothing yourself and only warn others.

blocks.p: The test is **grave and imminent danger** to the vessel or to a person. If it is there, the call is MAYDAY. If you need help urgently but nobody is in that danger yet, it is **PAN-PAN**, the urgency signal. If you need nothing yourself and only want to warn others, it is **SÉCURITÉ**, the safety signal.

head: Call
When
Example
rows: Grave and imminent danger to the vessel or a life
Fire out of control; a guest who cannot breathe
Urgent, but no such danger yet
Engine dead, drifting offshore; dismasted with a sound hull; a broken arm
A container or a log adrift in the fairway

blocks.p: Judge the people as well as the boat: a sound yacht with a guest whose throat is swelling shut is in distress.

sections.title: PAN-PAN three times, then who, then you

qa.q: How do I make a PAN-PAN call on the VHF?
qa.a: On channel 16 say **PAN-PAN** three times, ALL STATIONS (or the one station you want) three times, THIS IS and your name three times; then your position, what is wrong, the help you need, and OVER.

blocks.p: Make the call on channel 16. Say **PAN-PAN three times**, then the station you are calling three times, then THIS IS and your own name three times. ALL STATIONS reaches everyone in range. If only one station needs to hear you, name it instead: PAN-PAN three times, then Olympia Radio three times.

fig.title: On channel 16
lines: Engine failed, drifting. I need a tow

blocks.p: After the opening comes the message, in the order a rescuer needs it: **your position**, what is wrong, what help you want. Then OVER, and listen.

blocks.rule: PAN-PAN ×3 · who you call ×3 · THIS IS · your name ×3 · position · problem · help needed · OVER

sections.title: Stay on watch, cancel or upgrade

qa.q: When should I cancel a PAN-PAN, and when upgrade it to MAYDAY?
qa.a: **Upgrade to MAYDAY** the moment the danger becomes grave and imminent. If the problem goes away, say the engine starts again, cancel the PAN-PAN by telling all stations you need no help, so nobody keeps looking for you.

blocks.p: Once a coast station has your call, stay reachable: keep a listening watch on 16, or on the channel it gave you, until help arrives. If the problem goes away, say the engine starts again, **cancel** the PAN-PAN: tell all stations you need no help, so that nobody keeps looking for you.
If things get worse, do not wait. The moment the danger becomes grave and imminent, **upgrade to MAYDAY**.

fig.note: No engine, drifting onto a lee shore

blocks.cap: Nothing stops the drift: the danger is now grave and imminent, so the PAN-PAN becomes a MAYDAY.

qa.q: How do I get a doctor's advice over the VHF?
qa.a: Make a PAN-PAN **asking for medical advice** on 16; the coast station moves you to a working channel and puts you through to a doctor. Have the patient's age, symptoms and the first aid given ready.

blocks.p: An injury or illness that needs a doctor's view, but does not threaten life right now, is a PAN-PAN **asking for medical advice**. The coast station acknowledges on 16 and usually asks you to change to a working channel. Change, and carry on there: long urgency traffic moves off 16 to keep it free. The station then puts you through to a doctor.

head: The doctor needs
For example
rows: Conscious? Breathing normally? Where is the pain?
What you have done and any medicine given

blocks.p: A patient who is getting worse by the minute or struggling to breathe is a life in grave and imminent danger: that is MAYDAY.

sections.title: Announce on 16, warn on a working channel

qa.q: How do I warn other boats on the VHF about a container adrift?
qa.a: Announce it on 16: **SÉCURITÉ** three times, ALL STATIONS, your name, what the warning is about and which working channel to listen on. Then give the warning itself on that working channel.

blocks.p: **SÉCURITÉ** introduces a navigational or weather warning. Coast stations use it for gale warnings and dangers to navigation. Any station may send one, your yacht included: for a drifting container, a mooring buoy adrift in a harbour approach, an unlit mark.

Channel 16 carries only the announcement: what the warning is about and which working channel to listen on. The message itself goes out on that working channel. When a coast station announces a gale warning on 16 and names a channel, switch to that channel and listen.

sections.title: Who gives way on the air

qa.q: What do I do if a PAN-PAN breaks in while I am sending a SÉCURITÉ?
qa.a: Stop, listen and note it: calls rank in a fixed **priority**, distress, urgency, safety, routine, and the higher one takes the channel. Finish your SÉCURITÉ later, when 16 is clear.

blocks.p: Calls rank in a fixed order, and the higher one takes the channel. If a PAN-PAN breaks in while you are giving a SÉCURITÉ, stop, listen and note it, and finish your message later, when 16 is clear.

head: Rank
Signal
Other stations
rows: Keep off the channel unless they are helping
Give way and listen: they may be able to help
Listen; routine calls wait until it ends

blocks.p: Safety traffic comes before routine calls but imposes no radio silence. If a coast station is reading a SÉCURITÉ when you want to call a friend, wait until it ends, then make your call.
